doc.title: Hubert Laws — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Mongo Santamaria and early recording sessions
title: Bobby Timmons's Got to Get It
summary: Laws does not recall a Bobby Timmons date but suspects Tom McIntosh recruited him. He says he often plays Timmons's tune Dat Dere.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: Like you said about jazz, it’s a demanding profession. Here was a session – a date that really caught my eye was Got to Get It, Bobby Timmons
I played? I don’t remember that at all.
Jimmy Owens on it, James Moody, Joe Farrell, George Barrow, Bobby Timmons, piano, Eric Gale, Ron Carter, Billy Higgins.
Tom McIntosh was the arranger and conductor.
That’s probably why I did it, because of him. He probably got me engaged in that.
Then continuing – so, no recollection about Bobby? Because Bobby’s so funky. He was straight out of the church.
I play his tune all the time. I just played it the other night. Dat Dere. We played that, recorded it. We played it the other night.
So that’s what I was just wondering, if . . .
